clue.text: Puzzle made up by married American during social gathering

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so these letters go within the gathering

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for work or fun, as in a sewing bee
M is the standard abbreviation for married
US, as in United States

explanation.surface: A guest is baffled by a married American they meet at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemuse someone is to confuse or bewilder them, so it is a verb synonym of puzzle.

clue.text: Book a quiet room once more in German spa town

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
a den is a private retreat or study
the first three pieces said again

explanation.surface: A traveller reserves a peaceful room again at a German resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Baden is a famous spa resort in the Black Forest of south-west Germany.

clue.text: Bishop in power, her ideal man?

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: might is strength or power
Right Reverend, a bishop's title, abbreviated RR

explanation.surface: Asks whether a powerful bishop could be the perfect partner for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Right Reverend is the formal style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the idiomatic name for the perfect husband a woman hopes to meet.

clue.text: Clip tail of frigate bird

parts.note: to clip is to snip

indicators.note: the tail is the back end, so only the last letter of the ship's name is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Trimming the tail feathers of a frigate bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A frigate bird is a real seabird, which makes 'frigate bird' look like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The snipe is a long-billed wading bird of marshes and wet meadows.

clue.text: Ring embassy revealing oversight

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A phone call to an embassy exposes some official blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out by mistake, which is exactly an oversight.

clue.text: Injure quiet girl in plant

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
sh is the call for silence
Marigold is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a silent girl among the shrubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold, or kingcup, is a yellow-flowered wetland plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Pallets may be compared with something else

definitions.meaning: first meaning: piled one on another in a warehouse
second meaning: measured against a rival, as in how it stacks up

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition completes a sentence about pallets; the second uses the idiom of how one thing stacks up against another.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallets are piled in stacks, and to stack up against something is to be judged in comparison.

clue.text: I'm finished with old painting technique

parts.note: taken as written
something finished is past
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An artist declares they are done with an outdated method of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying on paint thickly so brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née, used before a woman's maiden name, means born
d. is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A short life story of someone who lived and died poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is a state of want or destitution, a noun synonym for poverty.

clue.text: Pistol produced by the German impostor

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
a ringer is someone passing themselves off as another, especially in sport

explanation.surface: A gun turns up in the hands of a German fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket handgun, named after its American maker Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Cotton on to what a paparazzo wants to do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grasp or understand

definitions.text: what a paparazzo wants to do
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: to obtain a photograph

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on to' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'to' is a link; the second half takes the idiom at its word for a press photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the picture is an idiom for understanding, as is the informal phrase to cotton on.

clue.text: Former partner leaving model more than enough

indicators.note: when someone is leaving they go away, so those letters are taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: a model to follow is an example
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: An ex walks out on a fashion model, which is more than enough drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the former partner from the start of the word for model.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, having plenty or even a surplus of something.

clue.text: Minor tremors, nothing to write home about

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: shakes that are not great ones
second meaning: the idiom for something unremarkable

explanation.surface: A small earthquake barely worth mentioning in a letter home.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition takes the idiom at its word: tremors that are not big are no great shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no great shakes' means mediocre or unimpressive, just like 'nothing to write home about'.

clue.text: Referring to private discussions with a judge (Brahmin caste upset at being excluded)

definitions.text: Referring to private discussions with a judge

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a different order
what is excluded is left out, so those two letters are removed first

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters come out

explanation.surface: A Hindu priestly class is offended at being shut out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits outside the brackets and the wordplay inside them; take one A and the T out before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing held in chambers takes place in the judge's private rooms rather than in open court.

clue.text: Popped into a church in a cradle of Christianity

indicators.note: something popped has burst apart, so the word beside it is scattered into a new order and dropped in

parts.note: taken as written
the word itself, rearranged
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone nipped into a church in one of the early Christian centres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a plain preposition but supplies the letters that go inside A and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in ancient Syria was an early Christian centre, where followers were first called Christians.

clue.text: Badly lit Korean vessel

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship from Korea is sailing with poor lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil tanker is a ship built to carry oil in bulk, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Continuing in the same way too, after a short time

parts.note: 'and' and 'too' both add something further
soon means after a short while

explanation.surface: A description of carrying on likewise, with something more to follow shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: 'And so on' is the phrase used to say a list continues along the same lines.

clue.text: Cover of old record bearing novel novel

indicators.note: novel here means new or unusual, so the following word is made new in a fresh order
a thing bearing something carries it, so the record holds the other letters within

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is an old record format
the word itself, rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes the sleeve of a vintage disc that tells an original story.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the trick: the first 'novel' means new and signals rearrangement, the second is the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or surround completely, a verb sense of cover.

clue.text: Carriers of disease — five seen by worried escort

indicators.note: a worried thing is agitated and shaken about, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for five
the word itself, rearranged

explanation.surface: Five infected people are spotted by an anxious chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a vector is an organism, such as a mosquito, that transmits an infection.

clue.text: One gorgeous girl hooking male in charge

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for male
an attractive young woman can be called a peach

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman snares a man who is running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is only a link and 'charge' alone is the definition. The girl hooks the male onto her front.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to formally accuse or charge them with misconduct.

clue.text: Greed shown by girl with diamonds round front of robe

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the girl and the gems sit on either side

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: the front of a word is its beginning, so only the first letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman in jewels over her gown is seen as grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl and diamonds together go round the single letter, so it ends up between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for money or possessions.

clue.text: Take a risk in seance with monarch appearing spookily

indicators.note: a ghostly appearance is weird and unsettled, so the letters of the two words come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medium gambles that a dead king will materialise during the seance.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance one's arm is a British idiom for attempting something risky in hope of success.

clue.text: Strangely frightening in middle of Great Lake

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central part, so only the centre letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the word
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Something spooky happening out on one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Lake' reads as one name, but the first word only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something weird in a way that unsettles or frightens.

clue.text: wBox blows up

definitions.note: the source prints a stray 'w' before the definition word Box

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer's punches come back up.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints a stray 'w' before 'Box'; the clue is just 'Box blows up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice without full force.

clue.text: Cheap wine from place operating close to landmark

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
a machine that is operating is on

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bar near a famous monument serves rough house wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonk is British slang for cheap, low-quality wine.

clue.text: Submerged launch subjected to enemy attack

parts.note: something submerged is under the water
to launch a missile is to fire it

explanation.surface: A submarine launches a torpedo and comes under attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under fire means being shot at by the enemy, or figuratively criticised.

clue.text: Kept private

definitions.meaning: first meaning: held back or set aside, as a table is
second meaning: reticent, not showing one's feelings

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about secrecy, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved seat has been kept for someone, and a reserved person is private and undemonstrative.

clue.text: Soldiers' former tax break

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a cess was an old local tax or levy

explanation.surface: Troops once had a tax holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or interval, such as a school break or a parliamentary holiday.
